sections.overview: The common whitethroat is a migratory songbird that breeds across much of Europe and western Asia and winters in sub-Saharan Africa.
sections.identification: Its white throat and rusty edges on the wing feathers help distinguish it from other small warblers.
sections.habitat: It favors open or semi-open places with low, dense shrubs and taller grasses.
sections.diet: It eats mostly insects and other small invertebrates during breeding, adding berries later in the year.
sections.behavior: Males often sing from an exposed perch above the scrub.
sections.reproduction: It builds a low nest in dense vegetation; both parents incubate and feed the young.
sections.ecology: It is a long-distance migrant, and its breeding habitat depends on maintaining early scrub growth and field-edge vegetation.
sections.conservation: In France it is listed as Near Threatened among breeding birds, with long-term decline and marked fluctuations reported.
